body.estimand_functional: \((\widehat\theta,\widehat\tau_R)=(\widehat y(\widehat M)_r^+\widehat B,\ q^\top\{\widehat s_1-\widehat y(\widehat M)_r^+\widehat B\})\), with root-\(K\) influence \((\Phi_{\theta},\Phi_\tau)\)

sampling_model.design: A fixed set of target-pre, donor-pre, donor-post, and target factual-post cells is observed; treatment histories and grid times are fixed.
sampling_model.units: Each cell contains \(K\) independent individuals, and cell samples are mutually independent.
sampling_model.treatment: The target switches treatment after the pre period, while donor units remain under control; exact donor-span transport identifies the target's untreated post-period survival row.
sampling_model.overlap: Conditional censor survival is at least \(g>0\) through every required cell horizon.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold cross-fitting estimates conditional event and censor survival. Besides \(a_K\to0\), \(b_K\to0\), and \(a_Kb_K=o(K^{-1/2})\), the event learner is normalized at the follow-up origin, its relative-survival error path \(R_{cf}\) is almost surely of bounded variation, and \(\max_{c,f,\ell}\|V_{cf\ell}(X)\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\). This variation condition is a substantive learner-class restriction, not a consequence of the ordinary product-rate assumption.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 identify the donor-span counterfactual and give finite-sample consistency for Kaplan--Meier spectral SSC under non-informative censoring.
Theorem 2 gives pointwise and uniform asymptotic linearity for one cross-fitted doubly robust treatment-specific survival curve.
Theorem 2 and Corollary 2 give row-space out-of-sample prediction guarantees for minimum-norm principal component regression.
Equation (4.12) gives the Fr\'echet derivative of the Moore--Penrose inverse under locally constant rank.
Sections 3--4 show interpolation, variance, and survival-curve bias for synthetic survival individuals.
Theorem 3.1 gives feasible inference for low-rank linear functionals when the working rank overestimates the true rank.

Theorem 2.1 recovers the factor space for bounded working rank at least the true rank as the cross-sectional dimension grows, and Theorem 3.2 with Corollary 3.1 gives over-estimated-rank-robust factor-augmented inference.

body.tldr: The augmented-IPCW cell score has an exact orthogonality identity, but the usual event-ratio and inverse-censor convergence rates alone do not deliver the claimed product remainder. The missing quantity is the total variation of the foldwise relative-survival path \(R_{cf}\). Under event-origin support, learner normalization, bounded variation, and the substantive rate \(\max_{c,f,\ell}\|V_{cf\ell}(X)\|_2=O_P(a_K)\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives the required \(O_P(a_Kb_K)\) cell bias and supplies the repaired premise for spectral counterfactual and grid-RMST inference. Without that restriction, an oscillatory-hazard sequence violates root-\(K\) centering even though the frozen product-rate condition holds.

project_justification.gap: Synthetic Survival Control identifies a clinically relevant low-rank counterfactual but assumes non-informative censoring and provides no influence-function limit law. Existing orthogonal survival-score rates do not by themselves control the Stieltjes variation that appears when those scores feed a learned panel map.
project_justification.niche: With fixed panel dimensions and many independent patients per cell, the cellwise survival problem is semiparametric, while the final counterfactual is a smooth multi-block spectral functional. The bridge requires both the complete pseudoinverse derivative and explicit path-variation control for the fitted event-survival ratio.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact augmented-IPCW Stieltjes remainder, exposes a necessary bounded-variation learner restriction and its \(L_2\) rate, and shows how the resulting joint cell influence vector feeds spectral, multiplier-band, and grid-RMST calculations. It also characterizes the unadjusted Kaplan--Meier/PCR probability limit and its fixed-bias region.

body.related_work: Han and Shah (2025) supply the low-rank survival-panel estimand, donor transport, and TCL application, but their Kaplan--Meier theory assumes non-informative censoring and points to IPCW as future work. Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024) supply the augmented survival-score architecture and single-law nuisance metrics, but those metrics alone do not control the total variation of the relative-survival Stieltjes integrator required here. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025) clarify minimum-norm PCR and row-space transport without censoring-aware asymptotics. Golub and Pereyra (1973) provide the constant-rank pseudoinverse differential used as a technique ancestor. Curth, Poon, Nori, and Gonz\'alez (2024) motivate censoring-bias analysis in survival synthetic controls but do not derive this informative-censoring PCR pseudo-limit or its relatively open nonzero-bias region. Fan and Liao (2022) study factor-space recovery in growing panels, not the fixed-donor, weak-gap pseudoinverse problem considered here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The positive theory is fixed-dimensional and, at the cell layer, applies only to event-survival learners whose relative-survival paths satisfy the stated bounded-variation and \(L_2\) variation-rate restrictions. Ordinary supremum or \(L_2\) consistency of survival ratios does not imply this property, so generic oscillatory learners are outside the theorem. The theory also does not cover a growing post grid, a shrinking singular gap, a selected rank, covariance degeneracy, or continuous-time RMST; the RMST target is exactly the fixed-grid functional \(q^\top(s_1-\theta)\).
body.honest_scope: The exact score identity shows that neither nuisance contributes a first-order term, while Cauchy--Schwarz supplies the product remainder only after the relative-survival variation rate is imposed. The joint-cell lemma therefore remains formally open until that substantive restriction is installed; the downstream spectral limit, multiplier band, and grid-RMST interval inherit it transitively. No variation or origin condition is imposed on the purely algebraic pseudoinverse differential or on the unadjusted Kaplan--Meier/PCR cancellation result. The weak-gap and rank-selection frontier remains an explicit open-ended question.
